newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit hovers at 2.51, seen retreating in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit hovers at 2.51, seen retreating in Europe.

text.p: The ringgit traded around 2.51 to a dollar for most of the Asian afternoon, but was expected to ease in European time unless Bank Negara intervened, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said fear of Bank Negara intervention, Malaysian corporate selling and triggering of some stop-losses were holding the ringgit from dipping further.
"It should break through 2.51 once we are closed," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur.
He said some U.S. funds were consistently selling the ringgit.
A Singapore-based analyst said Bank Negara was rumoured to be checking for quotes in the market, but was not likely to intervene immediately.
There was no confirmation as Bank Negara does not comment on its market operations.

"I think the central bank's strategy is to let go if the pressure is too heavy. It will come in later when it can be most effective with least amount of ammunition," a dealer with another Malaysian bank said.
At 0830 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5095/5105 a dollar.
